note: Initial canonical competency model, extracted from fde-db-triage (Slice 5.1).

competencies.name: Problem framing
competencies.definition: Asks what 'wrong'/expected/when before digging; forms hypotheses before querying.
default_signals: Client questions asked before first query.
Time-to-first-question vs time-to-first-query.
Hypotheses stated explicitly before testing them.

default_anchors.5: Clarifying question to Dana BEFORE the first query AND explicit hypothesis-testing in queries (refund hypothesis quantified and rejected against actual numbers).
default_anchors.3: At least one clarifying question to Dana (even if generic), OR explicit hypothesis-testing queries — one of the two, not both.
default_anchors.1: No clarifying question to Dana AND queries dive straight at the bug without any hypothesis stated.

competencies.default_scoring_note: Score on the candidate's own framing evidence. A wrong final answer does NOT lower this score — process is process.

competencies.name: Data fluency
competencies.definition: Explores schema, finds the duplicates, quantifies the gap; does not accept the refund hint blindly.
default_signals: Progression of db.query calls from exploration to targeted aggregation.
Dedup query present in the final solution.
Refund hypothesis explicitly tested and rejected with numbers.

default_anchors.5: Progression from exploration → targeted dedup CTE → duplicate-fingerprint (HAVING COUNT > 1) verification AND refund hypothesis tested with actual numbers.
default_anchors.3: Ran a dedup query OR a fingerprint query (found the duplicates) but did not test the refund hypothesis numerically.
default_anchors.1: Only naive SUM queries; accepted the refund hint without querying for it.

competencies.name: Design under constraints
competencies.definition: Uses targeted queries over full scans; manages compute and token budget; reprioritizes after the requirement change.
default_signals: Constraint-spend trajectory (compute / tokens) stays below the displayed budgets.
Query selectivity (predicates on indexed columns, narrow projections).
Reprioritization observable after curveball 1.

default_anchors.5: Targeted queries with narrow projections and predicates on indexed columns; <5 compute-minutes consumed total; visible reprioritization after curveball.
default_anchors.3: Mostly targeted queries with some broad scans; constraint spend visible in the trajectory but not pathological.
default_anchors.1: Many broad scans / SELECT * with no projections; compute trajectory drains visibly; no constraint-awareness.

competencies.name: Execution
competencies.definition: Produces corrected figures that actually run and match ground truth — but credit correct diagnosis and sound method separately from final-figure precision.
default_signals: Deliverable correctness vs ground truth within ±2%.
Working dedup query or script committed to the workspace.
All four deliverable components present.

default_anchors.5: Correct root cause (duplicates) + figures within ±2% of ground truth + working dedup query + upstream idempotency-key recommendation.
default_anchors.3: Correct root cause AND sound method (dedup query actually run) but figures materially off for a specific identifiable reason — e.g. dedup'd correctly but missed the status='succeeded' filter so figures came back ~12% high; or correct figures but missing the bonus upstream-fix recommendation. The diagnosis and method are REAL; the figure is wrong for a nameable reason. This is genuinely mid, not a failure.
default_anchors.1: Wrong root cause (e.g. blamed refunds) OR naive uncorrected figures OR no working dedup query at all.

competencies.name: AI orchestration
competencies.definition: Uses the AI assistant to accelerate work but verifies its output against the data.
default_signals: ai.assistant usage events followed by verification queries.
Does not paste assistant output as final without checking.
Recovers gracefully if the token budget runs low.

default_anchors.5: Focused AI-assistant turn on the actual problem (e.g. SQLite dedup pattern) followed by a verification query against the data.
default_anchors.3: AI-assistant used, but on the wrong hypothesis (e.g. refund subtraction) OR not verified against the data.

competencies.name: Teamwork
competencies.definition: Engages the teammate, verifies the misleading hint rather than acting on it, escalates appropriately.
default_signals: Exchange in the team channel before acting on the refund hint.
Refund hypothesis tested against the data, not just trusted.
Asks Sam follow-ups with specific evidence to unlock the real clue.

default_anchors.5: Engaged Sam in the team channel AND verified the refund hypothesis against data before acting AND pushed back with concrete numbers to unlock the webhook clue.
default_anchors.3: Engaged Sam, asked clarifying follow-ups, but accepted the refund hint without quantifying it against the actual gap.
default_anchors.2: Engaged Sam in some exchange (one or two messages) but accepted the misleading hint without any verification — or actively curt/dismissive but at least sent a reply.
default_anchors.1: No team-channel exchange at all (purely silent).

competencies.default_scoring_note: Score on the team-channel evidence directly. If the candidate genuinely engaged Sam in a multi-turn exchange, that is teamwork — even if they accepted the wrong hint, that lands them at 2-3, not 1.

competencies.name: Customer engagement
competencies.definition: Sets expectations, updates the anxious client, absorbs the requirement change calmly.
default_signals: Cadence and quality of client-channel updates.
Calm, non-defensive response to curveball 1.
Translates technical findings into client-appropriate language.

default_anchors.5: Clarifying question upfront + calm/professional handling of the curveball + plain-language client-facing summary.
default_anchors.3: Clarifying question OR calm curveball handling but not both; professional tone throughout.
default_anchors.2: Minimal engagement (one message) OR absent entirely but not actively rude.
default_anchors.1: Zero client-channel engagement AND no client-facing summary, OR actively rude/dismissive/curt tone toward client.

competencies.name: Outcome communication
competencies.definition: Board-ready paragraph is clear, accurate, non-technical, with the correct number and plain cause.
default_signals: Final paragraph reads as board-appropriate prose.
Corrected number is stated clearly and matches the candidate's own query.
Cause is described in plain English without jargon.

default_anchors.5: Board-ready paragraph in plain English, correct figure cited, plain-language root cause, upstream-fix mention.
default_anchors.3: Clean professional prose stating the (wrong) figures and an (incorrect) cause — clarity is real but the conclusion is wrong. CAP at this band when the content is incorrect; clear prose for the wrong answer cannot score 5.
default_anchors.1: Terse one-liner OR no client-facing summary OR jargon-laden / unstructured.

competencies.default_scoring_note: Communication quality is structure, audience-fit, and clarity — scored independently of execution correctness. The CAP at 3 applies when the candidate confidently communicates an incorrect conclusion; the well-written-but-wrong case should land mid, not at the bottom.
